questions.stem: An HR Admin without the System Admin role can do what? (Choose three.)

options.text: Grant roles to users or groups

questions.explanation: HR Admin without System Admin can B=modify HR Administration Properties, D=create HR Criteria, and F=add users to HR groups. A=granting platform roles requires admin; C=resetting passwords requires admin; E=configuring business rules requires elevated/admin access.

questions.stem: After the HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role has been removed from the Admin role, how may a user with only the Admin role add members to HR groups?

options.text: The Admin must elevate their role to security_admin to add members to HR groups.
The Admin follows the same process as with any group membership change.
The Admin can no longer add members to HR groups.
The Admin must impersonate an HR Admin to add members to HR groups.

questions.explanation: After sn_hr_core.admin is removed from admin, a user with only the admin role C=can no longer add members to HR groups — only the HR Administrator can assign scoped HR roles and manage HR group membership.

questions.stem: In the Create Bulk Cases module, which Filter by options are available in the dropdown? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The Filter by dropdown in Create Bulk Cases offers B=Upload File, D=User Criteria, F=HR Profiles, and G=HR Criteria. Document Template, HR Service Template, and HR Template are not Filter by options in this module.

questions.stem: If you have both Admin and HR Admin roles and wanted to configure an Access Control for the Employee Relations Cases table, what must first be done?

options.text: Add the Delegated Developer role to your User record
From the User dropdown in the banner, elevate your role to security_admin
Manually add the security_admin role to your User record
Nothing would need to be done

questions.explanation: To configure an ACL for any scoped app table including Employee Relations Cases, B=elevate your role to security_admin from the User dropdown in the banner. Permanently adding the role to the user record and doing nothing are not the correct approaches.

questions.stem: What type of information does the HR Profile contain?
questions.explanation: The HR Profile contains A=personal employee data including position, home address, employment dates, and other HR-specific information. Group membership and roles are on the User record; login/department are on sys_user; passwords are never stored in profiles.

questions.stem: How many User Criteria Records may be applied to a single KB or KB Article?
questions.explanation: C=Unlimited user criteria records may be applied to a single knowledge base or article. There is no restriction on the number of user criteria applied; multiple criteria records expand the set of users who can access the content.

questions.stem: In the base ServiceNow instance, how are User Criteria used?

options.text: To control which users can access the HR Case application
To control what a user sees in the information and suggested reading widgets
To control read and write access to Knowledge bases and articles
To control which users can access the HR Service Portal

questions.explanation: In the base instance, User Criteria are used to C=control read and write access to Knowledge bases and articles. HR case access is controlled by HR roles; Service Portal access by client roles; ESC content targeting uses HR Criteria.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true for an HR application as it relates to the User [sys_user] Table and the HR Profile [sn_hr_core.profile] Table?

options.text: Only HR Profile table is required in HR.
Only the User table is required in HR.

questions.explanation: A=Both the User [sys_user] table and HR Profile table are required — User provides identity/authentication while HR Profile stores HR-specific employee data. Neither can function independently in HR Service Delivery.

questions.stem: In the base instance, what determines the conditions a Case must meet before it can be assigned to an agent?
questions.explanation: A=Matching Rules determine the conditions a case must meet before assignment to an agent or group, matching on criteria like department, location, or skill. Client Rules, ACLs, and Escalation Rules do not control initial case assignment conditions.

questions.stem: What role is required, at a minimum, to view confidential HR Profile data?
questions.explanation: The minimum role to view confidential HR Profile data is B=HR Basic [sn_hr_core.basic], which grants read access to HR cases and profile information. HR Admin and HR Manager have elevated access; LE Admin is for Lifecycle Events only; Basic is the minimum required.

questions.stem: What types of HR Document templates may be created in ServiceNow? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: HR-supported document template types are A=Document Templates (HTML-based, modern standard) and C=PDF document templates. B=Word document templates are explicitly not supported in HR Service Delivery. Text document templates do not exist as an HR type.

questions.stem: What are the advantages of removing the HR Admin role from the system Admin role after the HR Implementation tasks have been completed? (Choose two.)

options.text: This ensures that HR has control over further HR configurations.
The HR Admin role should remain a part of the system Admin role.
This ensures that confidential HR data is only accessible to users with an HR role.
It is not necessary because the system Admin always has access to all HR data.

questions.explanation: Advantages of removing HR Admin from System Admin: A=ensures HR has sole control over further HR configurations (separation of duties), and C=ensures confidential HR data is only accessible to users with an HR scoped role.

questions.stem: What does ServiceNow now call the HR application?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow's HR application is called D=HRSD (HR Service Delivery). HRDS, HRSM, and HRMS are not the official product name used by ServiceNow.

questions.stem: What defines an employee's access to the HR Service Portal / Employee Service Center?
questions.explanation: Employee access to the HR Service Portal / Employee Service Center is defined by D=Client Roles — scoped roles assigned to HR service consumers. User Criteria controls KB access; HR Criteria determines agent case-creation eligibility; group membership alone does not define portal access.

questions.stem: What kind of records do HR Requests create?
questions.explanation: HR Requests from the Service Portal or Employee Service Center create D=HR Cases, which track employee requests through fulfillment. HR Incidents, HR Files, and HR Problems are not valid record types in HR Service Delivery.

questions.stem: In the HR Guided Setup Module, why are some tasks locked in the Task view?

options.text: They require an elevated role to access.
They are deprecated tasks that should not be completed.
They require other tasks to be completed first.
They require a plugin to be activated first.

questions.explanation: Some tasks in HR Guided Setup are locked because D=they require a plugin to be activated first before the configuration task can be performed. They are not role-restricted, deprecated, or dependent on completing prior tasks.

questions.stem: Which of the following are examples of HR application scopes? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: HR application scopes include B=Human Resources: Core, D=Human Resources: Integrations, E=Human Resources: Lifecycle Events, and G=Human Resources: Service Portal. COE, Knowledge, and Global are not separate HR application scopes.

questions.stem: How can an HR Administrator or Content writer limit which employees will see content on the Employee Service Center?

options.text: All employees will see the same information
Client roles automatically limit what is visible to employees

questions.explanation: HR Admins and Content Writers limit ESC content visibility using D=HR Criteria, which targets content by employee conditions (location, department, type). User Criteria controls KB access; client roles grant portal access; all-employee content is not targeted.

questions.stem: If the Audience field has been configured on a Lifecycle Event Activity, what will the system do if the subject person does not meet the criteria for that Activity?

options.text: the activity must be manually closed by the HR professional
the Lifecycle Event will be canceled
the activity must be manually closed by the Subject person

questions.explanation: If the Audience field is configured on a Lifecycle Event Activity and the subject person does not meet the criteria, D=the activity is automatically skipped. The lifecycle event is not canceled; no manual closure is required.

questions.stem: The ServiceNow SIM methodology is based around what generic methodologies?
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow Implementation Methodology (SIM) is based on B=Agile and Waterfall generic methodologies, combining agile sprints with structured waterfall governance phases. Waterfall+RAD, Prince, and Scrum+XP are not the SIM foundation.

questions.stem: If an HR Services needs to be accessible to employees on the Employee Service Center, what field must be completed on the HR Service?
questions.explanation: To make an HR Service accessible on the Employee Service Center, D=the Record Producer field must be completed — it links the employee-facing catalog item to the HR Service for self-service access. Checklist, Fulfiller Instructions, and Lifecycle Event type are not required for ESC visibility.

questions.stem: HR Profiles may be created for multiple employees using conditions and criteria in which module?
questions.explanation: HR Profiles can be created for multiple employees using conditions and criteria via C=Generate HR Profiles module, which allows bulk profile creation using custom criteria. Create Human Resources Profile creates a single profile; Bulk Cases creates HR cases not profiles.

questions.stem: User authentication and Instance restriction are examples of what type of security?
questions.explanation: User authentication (login controls) and Instance restriction (limiting access by IP/domain) are examples of D=Platform Access security — the layer controlling who can reach the instance. Physical Security is hardware protection; Roles and Groups is authorization-level; Contextual Security is record-level access via ACLs.

questions.stem:
If the HR Service does not have any Case options specified, HR Documents must be manually generated for the HR Case.
In this situation, who is able to generate an HR document for the Case?
questions.explanation: When no Case options are configured on the HR Service, documents must be manually generated. D=Only the assigned to person on the HR case can manually generate the HR document. Any HR professional, HR Admin only, and HR Manager only are not the correct roles for manual generation in this scenario.

questions.stem: When does the HR Template populate information on the HR Case form?

options.text: When the Opened for person is selected
When the Assignment group is selected.
When the HR Case Type is selected.
When the HR service is selected on the HR Case Creation form.

questions.explanation: The HR case template (HR Template) populates information on the HR Case form D=when the HR service is selected on the HR Case Creation form — it is linked to the HR Service and fires on service selection. It does not trigger on Opened For person, Assignment Group, or HR Case Type selection.

questions.stem: The HR Profile table is used to track information for what Employment types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The HR Profile table tracks C=Full Time Employee, D=Temporary Employee, and F=Contractor employment types for active workforce management. Other, Potential Employee, and Spouse are not standard HR Profile employment type values used in the HR Service Delivery application.

questions.stem: If the HRSD application is scoped, why can the System Administrator initially access all HR applications after the plugin has been installed?

options.text: When the HR plugins are installed, the necessary HR roles are added to the Admin role.
The roles were manually granted by a ServiceNow security user.
The Admin will always have access to all HR tables and data.
The roles were manually granted by an HR Admin.

questions.explanation: After HR plugin installation, the System Administrator can access all HR applications because A=the necessary HR roles are automatically added to the Admin role during plugin installation, enabling system configuration. The roles are not manually granted by security users or HR Admins; Admin does not inherently access scoped HR tables.

questions.stem:
Scenario: You have an existing ITSM customer who is now implementing HR Enterprise. In UAT, they discovered that they get an error message about a Read operation from the HR scope to the Global scope being denied. You have verified that each Script Include was written correctly.
What else must be done to allow the Script Includes to work in the HR application?

options.text: The Status of the associated record on the Application Restricted Caller Access list must be set to Denied.
You must create a custom ACL to allow the script includes to work.
The Status of the associated record on the Application Restricted Caller Access list must be set to Allowed.
You must change Scope for the script includes to work.

questions.explanation: When a scoped HR app calls a Global Script Include and gets a Read denied error, C=the Application Restricted Caller Access record for that Script Include must have its Status set to Allowed. Setting to Denied blocks access; a custom ACL does not resolve cross-scope caller restrictions; changing the Script Include scope would break global availability.

questions.stem: In the HR Guided Setup Module, the Configuration View displays which of the following for a Category? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: In HR Guided Setup, the Configuration View for a Category displays A=Properties, D=Lists, and F=Forms — the three panels for managing settings, record lists, and form layouts. Gauges, Dashboards, and Overviews are not displayed in the HR Guided Setup Configuration View for a Category.

questions.stem: What method needs to be invoked from MatchingRuleProcessor class?
questions.explanation: The method that must be invoked from the MatchingRuleProcessor class is A=processAndGetCandidates, which evaluates matching rule conditions and returns agent/group candidates for assignment. processAndGetUsers, processAndGetList, and processAndGetArray are not valid methods on the MatchingRuleProcessor class.

questions.stem: If an HR Service will only be used internally by HR professionals, what is the minimum configuration needed?

options.text: HR Service, HR Template, and Record Producer.
HR Service, HR Template, Record Producer, and Lifecycle event type.

questions.explanation: For an HR Service used only internally by HR professionals, C=HR Service alone is the minimum configuration required. HR Template and Record Producer are needed only for employee self-service via the portal. A Lifecycle Event type is required for onboarding/transitions, not for basic internal-only services.

questions.stem: The Knowledge bases searched for the Knowledge results section on an HR Case are determined by what?
questions.explanation: The knowledge bases searched for the Knowledge results section on an HR Case are determined by A=Contextual Search configuration, which maps tables/fields to knowledge bases for context-aware results. HR Service, HR Criteria, and Knowledge Management configuration do not directly control which KBs appear in the case search panel.

questions.stem:
When gathering requirements for HR Services, it is best to begin by defining the Service then working upwards, categorizing in progressively more detail.
What are the basic categories used?

options.text: HR Service, Topic Category, Activity Category, Activities, COE.
HR Service, Topic Detail, Topic Category, COE.

questions.explanation: When gathering requirements, define HR Service first then categorize upward: D=HR Service → Topic Detail (2nd-level) → Topic Category (1st-level) → COE (top). Activity Category/Activities are lifecycle event concepts; option A is missing Topic Detail; C is missing Topic Detail; B includes wrong elements.

questions.stem: If a knowledge base and its articles have no user criteria selected, a user without a role can do what?

options.text: can neither read nor contribute articles

questions.explanation: When a knowledge base and its articles have no user criteria configured, B=users without a role can read articles but cannot contribute. Read access defaults to open when no criteria is set; write/contribute access always requires a role such as knowledge or kb_contributor. Full restriction only applies when criteria explicitly blocks access.

questions.stem: How does ServiceNow know which HR Template to use on an HR Case?

options.text: The HR Template is referenced on the HR Service record.
The HR Template is referenced on the record producer form.
Each COE has a specific HR Template.
The HR Template is selected directly on the Catalog item.

questions.explanation: ServiceNow determines which HR Template to use on an HR Case via A=the Template field on the HR Service record, which references the HR case template that auto-populates case fields upon service selection. The template is not referenced on the record producer form, per-COE, or directly on the catalog item.

questions.stem: What are the key differentiators between an HR Profile record and a User record? (Choose three.)

options.text: The HR Profile stores the employee's assigned delegates.
The HR Profile includes group membership information.
The HR Profile includes employee organizational information like Colleagues.
The HR Profile stores login credential information.
The HR Profile may include employee marital status.
The HR Profile is intended to store confidential employee data that is pertinent for HR.

questions.explanation: Key differentiators of HR Profile vs User record: C=organizational info like Colleagues, E=personal data like marital status, F=confidential HR-specific data (salary, employment dates). User record stores login credentials (D), group membership (B), and delegate assignments (A) — those are platform-level fields, not HR Profile differentiators.

questions.stem: If a customer has a huge employee population, complex organizational structures, and requires custom integrations and language translations, what level of configuration complexity would their project be considered?
questions.explanation: A customer with huge employee population, complex organizational structures, custom integrations, and language translation requirements represents A=Drastic complexity — the highest HRSD implementation complexity level. Low and Nominal describe simple deployments; Major describes mid-tier complexity without all the advanced requirements listed.

questions.stem: When an employee completes a questionnaire on an Employee Form, on which table does the system store their answers?
questions.explanation: Employee Form questionnaire answers are stored in B=Metric Result [asmt_metric_result] table, since employee forms are built using the survey designer. sys_ui_form is the UI form configuration table; question_answer stores catalog variables; sn_hr_core_case stores HR case records, not questionnaire responses.

questions.stem: With the I18N: Knowledge Management Internationalization Plugin v2 enabled, how are translated Knowledge articles associated with each other so that the user is presented with the article in the selected language?
questions.explanation: With I18N Knowledge Management Internationalization Plugin v2 enabled, translated articles are linked via D=the Translated Versions related list, so users see the article in their selected language. Article Versions tracks revision history; Knowledge Feedback is for ratings; Affected Products is for product association.

questions.stem: When creating a PDF Document Template, where does the list of Document Revisions come from?
questions.explanation: When creating a PDF Document Template, the Document Revisions list comes from A=Managed Documents — PDF templates originate from Managed Documents (fillable or non-fillable PDFs uploaded and published there). Document Templates are HTML-based; Knowledge Articles and System Documents are not sources for PDF document revision lists.

questions.stem: Only users with which role, at a minimum, may view the confidential data on the HR Profiles table?
questions.explanation: The minimum role to view confidential data on the HR Profiles table is B=Profile Reader [sn_hr_core.profile_reader], which grants read access to profile data including sensitive information. Profile Writer adds write access; HR Case Writer/Reader are for case management and do not grant HR Profile table read access.

questions.stem: What determines if a user can view a Knowledge article?
questions.explanation: Whether a user can view a Knowledge article is determined by A=Can/Cannot Read User Criteria on the knowledge base or article — users must satisfy the "Can Read" criteria. Can/Cannot Contribute controls editing; HR Criteria controls HR case/portal access; ACL Rules are platform-level controls, not the primary KB article visibility mechanism.

questions.stem: What do Client Roles define?

options.text: Roles that come into force if user uses a browser client.
Named roles (eg VP of Operations, SVP Sales) for a customer’s clients.
Access for new hires, employees, alumni, contingent, and contract workers.

questions.explanation: Client Roles define D=access for new hires, employees, alumni, contingent, and contract workers within the HR application. They are not groups for the customer's clients, not browser-specific roles, and not named positional roles like VP or SVP — those are business titles, not ServiceNow Client Role classifications.

questions.stem: When a Guided Setup task is marked as complete, how can it be reopened?

options.text: Click the Mark as Incomplete button

questions.explanation: A Guided Setup task marked as complete can be reopened by B=clicking the Mark as Incomplete button, which resets the task so it can be reconfigured. Closed tasks can be reopened (A is false); submitting an HI request is not required; restarting the entire Guided Setup is unnecessary to reopen a single task.

questions.stem:
When creating a PDF Document template, the Document revision field must be completed.
How does the system determine which documents are available to be selected for this field?

options.text: You must be a member of the Owning Group for the Managed Document
Your group memberships and the Document owner field on the Managed Document record
You must have created the Managed Document record

questions.explanation: Documents available for the Document Revision field when creating a PDF Document Template are filtered by C=your group memberships and the Document owner field on the Managed Document record. Not all documents are visible; you are not required to have created the Managed Document; owning group membership alone is insufficient.

questions.stem: What is used to create a link on an HR Case form that accesses information outside the application?
questions.explanation: B=Link Generator is used to create links on an HR Case form that access information outside the application (external URLs or systems). HR Service defines fulfillment; Restricted Caller Access controls cross-scope scripting; COE Configuration organizes services — none of these generate external links on HR case forms.

questions.stem: When configuring a PDF Document Template, how does the system map form fields to ServiceNow fields?

options.text: The Document field type on the PDF Template Mappings record
The Preview value field on the PDF Template Mappings record
The Mapping field on the PDF Template Mappings record
The Document field on the PDF Template Mappings record

questions.explanation: When configuring a PDF Document Template, form fields are mapped to ServiceNow table fields via C=the Mapping field on the PDF Template Mappings record. Document field identifies the PDF form field name; Document field type specifies the type; Preview value shows a sample value — none perform the actual ServiceNow field mapping.

questions.stem: If the Match All field is checked on a User Criteria record, the user:

options.text: Must satisfy at least one of the criteria to meet the conditions.
Must satisfy at least of the criteria to meet the conditions.
Must satisfy a majority percentage of the criteria to meet the conditions.
Must satisfy all of the selected criteria to meet the conditions.

questions.explanation: When Match All is checked on a User Criteria record, D=the user must satisfy all of the selected criteria (AND logic). Without Match All, at least one condition is sufficient (OR logic). Options A and B describe OR logic; C (majority percentage) is not a valid User Criteria evaluation mode in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: If a new HR Knowledge base is created, how can it be included in the Knowledge results section on the HR Case form?

options.text: Add it to the HR Template
Add it to the HR Service configuration
All Knowledge bases are searched by default
Add it to the Contextual Search configuration

questions.explanation: To include a new HR Knowledge base in the Knowledge results section on the HR Case form, D=add it to the Contextual Search configuration, which maps knowledge bases to table/field contexts. Adding to HR Template or HR Service does not control Knowledge results; not all knowledge bases are searched by default.

questions.stem: How is the HR template associated with an HR service?

options.text: On the Lifecycle Event Activity Set

questions.explanation: The HR template is associated with an HR service via A=the Template field on the HR service record, which triggers auto-population of case fields when the service is selected. Association is not made on the Lifecycle Event Activity Set, on the HR template record itself, or directly on the HR case after creation.

questions.stem: Where does the HR Administrator define which HR Profile fields can be edited in the ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: The HR Administrator defines which HR Profile fields can be edited by users via B=HR Administration > Properties — specifically the "HR profile fields editable by users" setting. HR Profile > Setup and HR Profiles > Properties are not valid navigation paths; HR Administration > Setup is not the correct module for this configuration.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Owning Group field on the HR Template?

options.text: They approve the Template to be published.
They manage updates to the Template.
HR Cases are assigned to the Owning Group.

questions.explanation: The Owning Group on an HR Template identifies the group that C=manages updates to the Template — ownership governs who can create, update, or delete it. The owning group does not approve template publishing, own a Lifecycle Event, or receive HR case assignments; assignment groups are defined separately on the template.

questions.stem:
The Enterprise Service Management Integrations framework contains common components to be used for integrating HR applications with third-party systems.
Which capability does the Enterprise Service Management Integrations framework leverage to communicate with external instances and third-party systems?
questions.explanation: The Enterprise Service Management Integrations framework uses B=Flow Designer to communicate with external instances and third-party systems. Integration Designer, Design Hub, and Mobile Designer are not the capabilities leveraged by the ESM Integrations Framework for external communication.

questions.stem: What are some of the benefits of having separate COE tables? (Choose two.)

options.text: Allows for an extra layer of security within the HR organization.
Allows HR case agents to gather the right information based on the Service.
Eliminates the need for an HR case agent.
Eliminates the need to create database views.

questions.explanation: Benefits of separate COE tables include A=an extra layer of security within the HR organization (restricting cross-COE data access) and B=allowing case agents to gather the right information based on the Service (COE-specific fields). They do not eliminate the need for case agents or database views — both remain in use.

questions.stem: Who can generate the PDF document on an active HR Case?
questions.explanation: On an active HR Case, only A=the Assigned to person can generate the PDF document. The subject person's manager, HR Manager, and the employee (subject person) do not have permission to generate documents on active cases — generation is restricted to the assigned agent.

questions.stem: What role is required to access the modules in the HR Integrations application?
questions.explanation: The role required to access modules in the HR Integrations application is D=HR Integrations Admin [sn_hr_integrations.admin]. HR Lifecycle Event Case Writer, HR Core Profile Reader, and the generic Admin role do not grant access to the HR Integrations application modules.

questions.stem:
In the base ServiceNow platform, the Human Resources General Knowledge base has Can Contribute User Criteria set to Users with the [sn_hr_core.kb_write] role.
If a Knowledge article in the Human Resources General Knowledge base has no Can Contribute User Criteria set, what is the minimum role a user would need to edit the article?
questions.explanation: When an HR knowledge article has no Can Contribute User Criteria set, it inherits the KB-level criteria — the HR General KB requires D=KB Writer [sn_hr_core.kb_writer] role to contribute. HR Admin is a broader role; HR Basic also contains kb_writer but is a broader role; KB Reader grants only read access.

questions.stem: In which module can the HR admin manage the HR email address for incoming HR requests?
questions.explanation: The HR Admin manages the HR email address for incoming HR requests via D=HR Administration > Properties — HR properties include the inbound email address setting for HR case creation. HR Administration > Email Administration does not exist; System Properties > Email Setup/Properties are platform-level, not HR-specific email management.

questions.stem: In the base ServiceNow configuration, when are HR Cases created after a Bulk HR case request is submitted?

options.text: Twice per day using a scheduled job
Every 6 hours using a scheduled job
Once a day using a scheduled job

questions.explanation: In the base ServiceNow configuration, HR Cases are created D=immediately after a Bulk HR case request is submitted — cases are created synchronously upon submission. Scheduled jobs (twice per day, every 6 hours, once a day) are not used for bulk HR case creation in the base configuration.

questions.stem:
An employee in Chicago submits a request using the Employee Service Center. The HR Case template associated with the HR Service defines the Skills needed, but not an Assignment Group.
Using base platform functionality, which of the following is the first step the system takes to assign the Case?

options.text: An Assignment Rule creates a list of possible assignees
A Matching Rule assigns the Case to a group
The Case must be manually assigned
An Assignment Rule assigns the Case to a group

questions.explanation: When an HR Case template defines Skills but no Assignment Group, the first step is D=an Assignment Rule assigns the Case to a group — base Assignment Rules evaluate conditions to find the appropriate group. Matching Rules then narrow to individual candidates; manual assignment is not the first step; Assignment Rules assign groups, not lists of possible assignees.

questions.stem: Which of the following are predefined Dashboards that are installed with HR Case Management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Predefined dashboards installed with HR Case Management include A=Manager Dashboard, B=Overview, and F=HR Case Dashboard. Workforce Administration Dashboard, Onboarding Dashboard, and Employee Relations Cases Dashboard are not part of the base Case and Knowledge Management predefined dashboards.

questions.stem:
ServiceNow has identified 3 maturity levels for an HR customer.
What are they?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow identifies 3 HR customer maturity levels: A=Managed Interactions, Self-Reliance, and Smart Services — progressing from basic case management to self-service to AI-driven delivery. Other options contain incorrect level names: Self-Help, Advanced Services, No automation, and Automated Services are not the defined maturity levels.

questions.stem: When using the Generate HR Profiles module to create HR Profiles, what field must be completed to ensure the employees are granted the appropriate Client Role?
questions.explanation: When using Generate HR Profiles, A=Employment type must be completed — it determines which Client Role is granted, as each employment type (Full Time, Contractor, Alumni, etc.) maps to the appropriate HR client role. Profile type, Employee type, and User type do not drive Client Role assignment.

questions.stem: What does the employee utilize when submitting a self-service request to the HR Organization?
questions.explanation: Employees submitting self-service requests to HR use A=HR Catalog — the HR service catalog accessed via the Employee Service Center. HR Skills are agent qualifications; HR Template auto-populates case fields; HR Profile stores employee data — none are the employee-facing interface for request submission.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of HR Topic Categories?

options.text: They group common HR Catalog Items.

questions.explanation: HR Topic Categories A=group common HR Services — they provide the first-level categorization of services under a COE (e.g., Benefits, Payroll). They do not group HR templates, employees, or catalog items directly; their purpose is organizing services by functional type for navigation and reporting.

questions.stem: What are the benefits of the HR application being scoped? (Choose three.)

options.text: Provides an additional layer of control over HR data.
Allows HR Admins to configure the HR application.
HR department has more autonomy to manage all aspects of HRSD.
Allows the System Administrator complete control.
HR department has full control of the global application.

questions.explanation: Benefits of the HR application being scoped include: A=additional layer of control over HR data, B=HR Admins can configure the HR application independently, and C=the HR department has more autonomy to manage HRSD. System Admin does not gain complete control (D); HR manages HR scope only, not the global application (E).

questions.stem:
The HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role allows the user to add members to groups.
What additional role is needed for an HR Admin to remove users from groups?
questions.explanation: While HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] can add members to HR groups, removing users additionally requires A=User Admin [user_admin] role. User Writer and User Reader are not standard ServiceNow roles; HR User Admin is not a valid base system role name.

questions.stem:
On the HR Case form, some HR Services have associated Response templates.
What determines which HR Services have Response Templates?

options.text: The HR Criteria on the HR Service
The HR Criteria on the Response Template record
The table and conditions on the Response Template record
The User Criteria on the HR Service

questions.explanation: Which HR Services show Response Templates on an HR Case form is determined by C=the table and conditions on the Response Template record — templates matching the case table and conditions appear automatically. HR Criteria on HR Service/Response Template and User Criteria on HR Service do not control Response Template availability.

questions.stem: At what level is User Criteria set to control who can read and edit knowledge articles?

options.text: In either the Knowledge Base or Article.

questions.explanation: User Criteria controlling read/edit access to knowledge articles can be set at A=either the Knowledge Base level or the individual Article level — both levels support Can/Cannot Read and Can/Cannot Contribute criteria. The User record does not hold criteria; it is not limited to KB-only or article-only configuration.

questions.stem: How many COEs may be associated with an HR Service?
questions.explanation: Only B=1 COE may be associated with an HR Service — each HR service belongs to exactly one Center of Excellence, defining its categorization and security. Multiple COEs cannot be associated with a single service; 5, 10, and unlimited are all incorrect.

questions.stem: Which module provides a user-friendly interface for creating new HR Skills and assigning HR skills to members of the HR department?
questions.explanation: C=Manage HR Skills module (HR Administration > Manage Roles > Manage HR Skills) provides the interface for creating HR Skills and assigning them to HR department members. Skills Routing routes cases by skill; Skills Management is not the HR module name; Skills Definition is not a valid module.

questions.stem: Which table is considered the core table for all HR Case records?
questions.explanation: D=HR Case [sn_hr_core_case] is the core table for all HR Case records — all COE-specific case tables (payroll, benefits, etc.) extend it. Skill [cmn_skill] and Incident [incident] are unrelated; HR Task stores task records; HR Profile stores employee information.

questions.stem: Which HR Role is typically granted to all HR Support staff, at a minimum?
questions.explanation: B=HR Basic [sn_hr_core.basic] (HR Agent) is the minimum role granted to all HR support staff — it provides daily work access including case writing, KB writing, profile writing, and skills. HR Admin is elevated config access; KB Writer and Document Management User are sub-roles contained within HR Basic.

questions.stem: A user with only the HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role can save and modify which copies of existing reports?
questions.explanation: A user with only HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role can save and modify D=Personal copies of existing reports. Group-level reports require report_group or equivalent; Global reports require admin/report_admin; HR Admin alone does not grant group or global report publishing rights.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a configuration and a customization?

options.text: Configuration uses complex JavaScript while Customization involves field name changes and new buttons.
There is no difference between Configuration and Customization.
Customization uses the built-in tools in the platform while Configuration involves code changes.
Configuration uses the built-in tools in the platform while Customization involves code changes.

questions.explanation: D=Configuration uses the platform's built-in tools (form layouts, Flow Designer, UI Builder) while Customization involves code changes (script modifications, custom Script Includes). The reverse is incorrect (A, C); there is a clear and meaningful difference between the two approaches (B is false).

questions.stem: Which Service Portal configuration option is used to customize the logo, theme, and title of the HR Service Portal?
questions.explanation: The option used to customize the logo, theme, and title of the HR Service Portal is D=Branding Editor. Designer handles page layout; Page Editor modifies page content; Widget Editor customizes individual widgets — none control portal-level branding elements like logo, theme, and title.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to access the HR Properties module?
questions.explanation: The minimum role to access the HR Properties module is D=HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin]. HR Manager has case/profile access but not administration configuration rights; LE Admin manages Lifecycle Events; generic Admin is not the minimum HR-scoped role required for HR Properties.

questions.stem: The HR Case [sn_hr_core_case] table is an extension of what?
questions.explanation: The HR Case [sn_hr_core_case] table is C=an extension of the Task table [task] — ServiceNow uses Task as the base for all work items including HR cases. It is not an extension of Incident, the Case table from Customer Service Management, or the Lifecycle Events table.

questions.stem: What role is required to assign scoped HR roles?
questions.explanation: A=HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] is the only role that can assign scoped HR roles to users. HR Manager has elevated case/profile access but cannot assign scoped roles; LE Admin manages lifecycle events; HR Basic is the minimum frontline agent role without role-assignment capability.

questions.stem:
The customer you are implementing has purchased HR Service Delivery Enterprise which includes Enterprise Onboarding and Transitions.
Which plugin must be activated to utilize Enterprise Onboarding and Transitions?

options.text: Human Resources Scoped App: Lifecycle Events [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events]

questions.explanation: To utilize Enterprise Onboarding and Transitions, A=Human Resources Scoped App: Lifecycle Events [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events] must be activated. Employee Document Management is an optional add-on; HR Core is a prerequisite but not the EOT-specific plugin; Employee Service Center provides the portal, not the onboarding workflow engine.

questions.stem: The Lifecycle Events [sn_hr_le_case] table is a direct extension of which table?
questions.explanation: The Lifecycle Events Case [sn_hr_le_case] table is a direct extension of C=HR Case [sn_hr_core_case], the core table for all HR case records. Talent Management and HRIT Operations Case extend HR Case but are not the LE table's parent; sc_task is a service catalog task, not the direct parent.

questions.stem: Delegated Developers are granted access only to what in which they are working?
questions.explanation: Delegated Developers are granted access only to D=Scopes — the specific application scopes they are assigned to develop within. They cannot access other scopes, interfaces, APIs, or instances beyond their delegated scope, enforcing development responsibility boundaries.

questions.stem:
The customer you will be implementing for wants to utilize Now Mobile.
What is the minimum HR SKU they may purchase that includes Now Mobile?

options.text: Now Mobile is a standalone solution

questions.explanation: A=HR Service Delivery Professional is the minimum HR SKU that includes Now Mobile for HR. Now Mobile is not a standalone solution; HR Standard does not include it; HR Enterprise also includes it but Professional is the minimum required SKU for Now Mobile access.

questions.stem: If the HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] needs to develop within the HR application but cannot have the system Admin role, what additional role should be granted?
questions.explanation: If an HR Admin needs to develop within the HR application without System Admin, C=Delegated Developer [delegated_developer] role must be granted — it provides development access to specific application scopes without full system admin. HR Basic and HR Manager are operational roles; Scoped Developer is not a valid role name.

questions.stem:
When a Document Template is created from an HR Case, the name of the person who created the document is added to the name of the attachment.
Why?

options.text: It indicates who should sign the document
It indicates who generated the document
It indicates the Opened for user
It indicates who the document is about

questions.explanation: When a Document Template is created from an HR Case, the creator's name is appended to the attachment name to B=indicate who generated the document, enabling traceability. It does not indicate who should sign, the Opened for user, or the document subject — the generator is identified for audit purposes.

questions.stem: How can fields for a specific HR Service be displayed on the New Case Creation page?

options.text: HR Service-specific fields cannot be added to the New Case Creation page
Using the Case Creation Service Configurations
Using the Case Options field on the HR Service

questions.explanation: HR Service-specific fields can be displayed on the New Case Creation page by B=using the Case Creation Service Configurations, which control which fields appear per service during case creation. HR Service-specific fields can be added (A is false); Case Options control document generation; HR Criteria controls access eligibility.

questions.stem: Which field on the HR Service record defines which HR Catalog Item is associated with the Service?
questions.explanation: D=Record Producer field on the HR Service record defines which HR Catalog Item is associated with the service for employee self-service. COE categorizes the service; Topic Detail provides 2nd-level categorization; Template links the HR case template — none define the catalog item association.

questions.stem: What must be updated or loaded into the Customer's instance before importing the stories?
questions.explanation: Before importing Agile stories into a customer's instance, C=Products must be updated or loaded first — products are the parent container for epics and stories. Backlogs and Epics depend on Products; Groups are unrelated to story import hierarchy. Products are the prerequisite for story import operations.

questions.stem: When the Lifecycle Events application is installed, the LE Admin role is granted to which role?

options.text: It is not added to other roles

questions.explanation: When the Lifecycle Events application is installed, the LE Admin [sn_hr_le.admin] role is automatically granted to A=HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin]. It is not added to HR Basic or HR Manager; it is not a standalone role — HR Admins automatically receive LE Admin upon Lifecycle Events installation.

questions.stem: Which of the following applications is installed with the Human Resources Scoped App: Core plugin?
questions.explanation: D=HR Case Management is the application installed with the Human Resources Scoped App: Core plugin [com.sn_hr_core]. Employee Service Center [com.sn_hr_service_portal], Employee Document Management, and Lifecycle Events [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events] are separate plugins activated independently.

questions.stem: If you wanted someone to administer the Employee Service Center without granting them the HR Admin role, which scoped Admin role would they need?
questions.explanation: To administer the Employee Service Center without the HR Admin role, A=Service Portal Admin [sn_hr_sp.admin] scoped admin role is required. Widget Admin, Employee Files Admin, and Integrations Admin manage different application areas and do not grant Employee Service Center administration rights.

questions.stem: When does the platform assign a Client Role to a user?

options.text: Client Roles must be manually added to each employee record
When an HR Profile is created or modified for the employee
Client Roles are automatically added with Group membership
When a User record is created for the employee

questions.explanation: Client Roles are automatically assigned B=when an HR Profile is created or modified — the platform evaluates HR Profile conditions to determine and assign the appropriate client role via the Update Client Roles scheduled job. Manual assignment is not required; group membership and User record creation do not trigger client role assignment.

questions.stem: If you had little coding experience and were tasked with adding new pages to the customer’s Employee Service Center, which Service Portal Configuration option would be best to complete the task?
questions.explanation: For adding new pages to the Employee Service Center with little coding experience, B=Designer is best — it provides a drag-and-drop visual interface for page creation without code. Page Editor is more technical; Widget Editor requires Angular/HTML knowledge; Branding Editor only adjusts portal branding elements.

questions.stem: What provides a graphical interface to create survey categories, questions, configure the details, and publish the survey?
questions.explanation: A=Survey Designer provides the graphical interface for creating survey categories, questions, configuring details, and publishing surveys. Survey Workflow automates post-completion actions; Survey Developer and Survey Portal are not standard module names for this survey authoring capability.

questions.stem: HR Administrators can configure a personal copy of the HR Case Dashboard using which of the following buttons? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: HR Administrators configure a personal copy of the HR Case Dashboard using A=Add Content (adds reports/widgets to sections) and D=Change Layout (adjusts column layout). Delete Content, Modify Layout, and Add Layout are not available dashboard configuration buttons in the base system.

questions.stem: What determines when the HR Chat queue is available?

options.text: Schedule field on the HR Profile
Schedule field on the User record
Schedule field on the Queues record

questions.explanation: HR Chat queue availability is determined by D=the Schedule field on the Queues record, which defines active hours. HR Profile and User record schedule fields are not used for chat availability; HR Chat is not always available — the Queue schedule controls when agents receive chats.

questions.stem: What defines the path the Case or HR Task will take when it is escalated?
questions.explanation: D=Escalation Rules define the path a Case or HR Task takes when escalated — specifying conditions, escalation target, and timing. Assignment Rules handle initial assignment; Business Rules are scripted server-side logic; Matching Rules match agents to cases by skills — none define the escalation path.

questions.stem: If the HR Administrator group has been tasked with collecting Performance Analytics data, what additional role should be granted to the group?
questions.explanation: To collect Performance Analytics data, the HR Administrator group should be granted A=Performance Analytics Data Collector [pa_data_collector] role. PA Administrator has full configuration rights; PA Threshold Admin manages thresholds; System Admin is not the targeted role for data collection tasks.

questions.stem: If the HR Administrator has only been given the HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role, what additional role is necessary for them to configure all aspects of the Employee Document Management application?
questions.explanation: To configure all aspects of Employee Document Management, C=EF Admin [sn_hr_ef.admin] role is required — it grants full control over the application including administration, document management, and role assignment. Document Writer/Reader grant limited access; HR Admin alone does not include EDM administration rights.

questions.stem: If both the Knowledge Base and the KB article have no "Can Read" User Criteria, what role is required to read the article?
questions.explanation: When both the Knowledge Base and the KB article have no Can Read User Criteria, C=no role is required to read the article — the absence of criteria makes the content accessible to any logged-in user without a specific role. HR Basic, HR Manager, and HR Admin are not prerequisites when no restricting criteria is set.

questions.stem: Using the base HRSD configuration with no integrations, when the subject person electronically signs an HR document or PDF document, the signature is saved as what?

options.text: a picture of the signature that is added to the document

questions.explanation: The drawn signature is captured as an image stored in the Signature Image [signature_image] table — not a digital certificate or key. Typing a name provides acknowledgement but does not capture an image.

questions.stem: What role needs to be removed from the Admin role at go live to prevent the System Admin from being able to see HR Profile information?
questions.explanation: Only users with an HR scoped role can view HR cases and profile data. Removing HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] from System Admin blocks access to HR Profile information — the other listed roles are not assigned to Admin by default.

questions.stem:
If you select Data Type Numeric Scale on the Assessment Metric (Survey Question) form there is a Scale definition field made visible.
What does it mean to select High for the Scale definition?

options.text: It means a high score is bad
It means a high score is good
There is no option for Scale definition
There is no option for High

questions.explanation: Scale definition 'High' means a high score is the positive/desirable outcome. 'Low' means a low score is better. This applies to Likert and numeric scale data types on Assessment Metric forms.

questions.stem: In which Application Scope is the Lifecycle Events table contained?
questions.explanation: The Lifecycle Events table is in the Human Resources: Lifecycle Events scope [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events] — a separate plugin from HR Core. HR Core covers cases and profiles; Service Portal and Integrations are distinct scopes.

questions.stem: What settings define and track cross-scope access to applications?
questions.explanation: Restricted Caller Access settings define and track cross-scope access to application tables and script includes. Caller Tracking logs access during development; Caller Restriction enforces it in production. Both are forms of Restricted Caller Access.

questions.stem: What determines which Knowledge bases, Knowledge articles, and Service Catalog Items an employee can view?
questions.explanation: User Criteria is the platform mechanism controlling access to Knowledge bases, Knowledge articles, and Service Catalog items. HR Criteria evaluates HR tables and can generate linked User Criteria, but User Criteria is the direct access filter.

questions.stem: The Template field referenced on the HR Service record is used to do what?

options.text: Populate fields on the HR Case record
Filter who can access the HR Service
Create pre-configured responses HR professionals can use
Make the HR Service accessible on the Employee Service Center

questions.explanation: The Template field references an HR case template that automatically populates fields on the HR case form when a request for that service is made. It does not filter access, create responses, or control portal visibility.

questions.stem: When is the Record producer field needed on the HR Service record?

options.text: When the HR professional will be creating Cases on behalf of the employee
When you want the employee to request the HR Service from the Employee Service Center
It is always a required field
There is no Record producer held on the HR Service record

questions.explanation: The Record producer field (labeled 'Employee self-service only') is needed only when employees request the service directly from the Employee Service Center or HR Service Catalog. HR-initiated cases do not require it.

questions.stem: What are the major HR Service Catalog components? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Creating an HR catalog item auto-creates HR Service (F), Record Producer (E), and HR case Template (A); the catalog item itself (C) is the fourth component. Assignment Group, Matching Rule, and HR Profile are not catalog components.

questions.stem: How can HR Tasks be marked as optional?

options.text: Set Optional to True on the HR Task Template
Set Optional to True on the Activity Set
Set Optional to True on the HR Case form

questions.explanation: Optional HR tasks are configured by setting Optional to True on the HR Task Template, allowing fulfillment agents to skip the task without blocking case resolution. The Optional field does not appear on Activity Sets or HR case forms.

questions.stem: What provides a graphical representation of other tables related to a specific table, either through class extension or reference?
questions.explanation: The Schema Map provides a graphical view of table relationships — class extensions (parent/child) and reference fields to other tables. Accessed via the Tables list or right-click Show > Schema Map. System Map and Table Map are not valid feature names.

questions.stem:
Scenario: An existing ITSM customer is now implementing HR Enterprise. As part of the implementation, the Scoped Application Restricted Caller Access [com.glide.scope.access.restricted_caller] plugin was automatically activated.
By default, what is the Caller Access field set to?
questions.explanation: When the Scoped Application Restricted Caller Access plugin activates, the Caller Access field defaults to Caller Restriction — blocking unauthorized cross-scope calls. Caller Tracking is a manual development-stage setting, not the default.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the key factor in determining the implementation timeline?
questions.explanation: Configuration complexity is the primary driver of implementation timeline — it determines the scope of design, build, test, and validation work. Integrations, customer location, and business type are secondary factors.

questions.stem: Beginning with the Orlando release, which module allows HR Administrators to define which groups may access the various COEs or HR Services without needing to edit or create new ACL records?
questions.explanation: COE ACL Configuration lets HR Administrators grant read/write access to HR cases per COE by group, without creating or editing individual ACL records. Example: block the Benefits group from viewing Compensation COE cases.

questions.stem:
Scenario: You have an existing ITSM customer who is now implementing HR Enterprise. In UAT, they discovered that a new button on the HR case, created using the Link Generator application, is not displaying the appropriate web page. Instead, they get a Page Not Found error. You have verified that the Link configuration and script are both accurate.
What else must be done to allow the Link to work?

options.text: The Status of the associated record on the Application Restricted Caller Access list must be set to Denied.
You must create a custom ACL to allow the link to work.
The Status of the associated record on the Application Restricted Caller Access list must be set to Allowed.
You must change Scope for the link to work.

questions.explanation: Link Generator is in a different application scope. Cross-scope calls are blocked by default; the record in Application Restricted Caller Access must have its Status set to Allowed. No ACL creation or scope change is needed.

questions.stem:
A customer using Lifecycle Events Enterprise has documented a large offboarding Lifecycle Event that includes many steps. Many of the steps, including approvals, must be completed in a specific order.
Which of these is the best method to use to ensure the activities are triggered in the appropriate order?

options.text: Create a new lifecycle event for each of the dependent items
Create separate trigger conditions for each of the dependent activities
Create activity containers for the dependent items
Create separate activity sets for each of the dependent activities

questions.explanation: Activity sets act as containers grouping activities with the same trigger conditions. For ordered execution, dependent activities are placed in separate activity sets with trigger scripts verifying prior sets are complete.

questions.stem: What kinds of records can be created using HR Service Activities? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: HR Service Activities create Approvals (B) and Tasks (D). Tasks are created via a Child task template; Approvals are another supported activity type. Workflows are separate automation objects; HR Templates are used within activities, not created by them.

questions.stem: Which HR Integrations module is used to document the URL, basic integration properties, and inbound and outbound username and password information for a third-party application?
questions.explanation: The Sources module stores the endpoint URL, basic integration properties, and SOAP credentials (inbound/outbound username and password) for third-party integrations. Schema Mapping and HR Webservices serve different purposes.

questions.stem: How can a PDF document on an active HR case be generated? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: PDF documents on an active HR case can be generated A=automatically when the HR service is configured with Document Template fulfillment, or D=manually by the Assigned to person from the case form. Managers and employees do not generate documents.

questions.stem: After configuration on a Lifecycle Event is complete, what additional configuration is needed to initiate the LE process for an employee?

options.text: None. The LE will automatically trigger based on its configuration
An Event is needed to initiate the LE process
A Scheduled Job is needed to initiate the LE process
An HR Service is needed to initiate the LE process

questions.explanation: After configuring a Lifecycle Event, an HR Service with Fulfillment type = Lifecycle Event must be created to initiate the LE process for employees. Without the HR Service, there is no trigger mechanism for the LE.

questions.stem: In Employee Document Management, which of the following statements is true for legal holds?

options.text: Legal Holds are permanent and cannot be removed
Legal Holds may be placed on a group of HR profiles
Legal Holds may be placed on either a Document Type or an individual employee’s HR Profile
Legal Holds may be manually placed on individual employee documents

questions.explanation: Legal Holds may be placed on either a Document Type (bulk) or an individual employee's HR Profile. They are not permanent — holds can be removed. Individual documents are not targeted directly; a group of profiles can also be held via bulk processing.

questions.stem: Each HR service created in _______ has a corresponding transform map job.
questions.explanation: Each HR service created in HR Integration Service has a corresponding transform map job that maps the HR service to the appropriate HR web service for integration. HR Schema Mapping maps fields; HR Outbound Schema Mapping identifies outbound data; HR Transform Maps is not a module name.

questions.stem: If the Workflow editor is utilized for a Lifecycle Event, how does the system know when a task or approval should be triggered?

options.text: The activity set trigger condition determines when it is triggered
Activities are automatically triggered on specific dates
The Activity trigger condition determines when it is triggered

questions.explanation: The activity set trigger condition determines when tasks and approvals in a lifecycle event are triggered. Trigger conditions define whether a set fires immediately, on a date, or via an advanced script.

questions.stem: What Primary Security aspects are focused on for the HR application? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three primary security aspects of the HR application are C=Contextual Security (record data context drives access), E=Roles and Groups (role-based access control for HR functions), and F=Platform Access (application scope and module access). Password Security and Physical Security are not HRSD-specific security focuses.

questions.stem:
A customer using Lifecycle Events Enterprise has configured their onboarding process. Now, management has tasked the HR Admin with creating a way to back out onboarding work in case the new employee decides not to join the company.
Which of these is the best method to use to reverse work already performed as part of this Lifecycle Event?

options.text: Check the “allow blackout” box on each of the activities
Configure a new Lifecycle Event with the necessary activities
Configure the rescind activity set with the necessary activities
Check the “allow blackout” box on each of the activity sets

questions.explanation: Configuring the rescind activity set with the necessary activities is the best method to reverse work already performed in a lifecycle event. Each rescind activity is linked to the specific activity it will undo. 'Allow blackout' and creating a new lifecycle event are not the correct approaches.

questions.stem: If the Applies to all services box is not checked on the COE ACL Configuration record, what additional configurations must be made to the record?

options.text: More than one group must be added to the Groups list
At least one HR Service must be selected for the Services list
An Applies when condition must be created for each Service

questions.explanation: When 'Applies to all services' is not checked, the Services field appears and at least one HR Service must be selected to define which services the security policy covers. No additional groups, conditions per service, or other fields are required by default.

questions.stem: If an HR Document must be manually generated for an HR Case, who is able to generate the document from the Case record?

options.text: Only an HR Admin can generate Documents from a Case
Any HR professional can generate the Document, even if they are not assigned to the Case
Only the assigned to person can manually generate Documents from a Case
Only the Manager of the assignment group can generate the Document

questions.explanation: Only the Assigned to person can manually generate a document from a Case record — the procedure requires opening an HR case that is assigned to you. HR Admin and other HR professionals who are not assigned cannot generate documents from that case.

questions.stem: What role is required at a minimum, to access the Lifecycle Events Cases View Dashboard?
questions.explanation: The LE Admin [sn_hr_le.admin] role is required at minimum to access the Lifecycle Events Cases View Dashboard and Onboarding Executive Dashboard. HR Case Reader and HR Basic roles do not grant access to LE dashboards; HR Admin alone does not include LE admin access.

questions.stem: Using the Lifecycle Event Enterprise application, tasks may only be assigned to... (Choose the most appropriate answer.)

options.text: Only users with a Client Role
Only users with an HR role
HR Case Workers. Employees, users in other groups
Only users with the Manager role

questions.explanation: With LE Enterprise, tasks may be assigned to HR case workers, employees, and users in other groups (cross-departmental teams) — enabling automation across IT, Facilities, and other departments. Basic Lifecycle Events limits to HR only.

questions.stem: What identifies data from HRSD to push to a third-party HR application?
questions.explanation: HR Outbound Schema Mapping identifies the data fields from HRSD source tables to push to a third-party HR application, mapping ServiceNow fields to the target system's fields.

questions.stem: When configuring the Onboarding Lifecycle Event, the HR Admin did not select an Audience for the 'Select a Desk' task. If a remote employee is being onboarded. how does the system handle this task?

options.text: The Lifecycle Event rescind process will be triggered
The Lifecycle Event will be canceled
The activity will be triggered and must be manually closed

questions.explanation: When no Audience is configured on an activity, it applies to all employees — including the remote employee. The 'Select a Desk' task will be triggered and must be manually closed by the assigned party since the audience was not restricted to in-office employees.

questions.stem: When configuring a record on the COE ACL Configuration module how can you apply the conditions to all HR services for the COE?

options.text: Add a filter condition for each HR service
Select the Applies to all services box
Write a new ACL record for each HR service
Select each HR service using the Services list

questions.explanation: Select the 'Applies to all services' checkbox to apply the COE security policy to all HR services under that COE at once. When unchecked, individual services must be selected from the Services list.

questions.stem: If you have both Admin [admin] and HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] roles and want to configure an Access Control Rule for the HR Payroll table, which of the following must first be done?

options.text: Manually add the Delegated Developer role to your User record
Manually add the security_admin role to your User record
From the User dropdown in the banner, elevate your role to delegated_developer
From the User dropdown in the banner, elevate your role to security_admin

questions.explanation: To configure an Access Control Rule for any table, elevate your role to security_admin from the User dropdown in the platform banner. This is a temporary elevation — permanently adding the role to a user record is not the recommended approach.

questions.stem: The customer has a group of developers who will be tasked with making subprod updates to the HR Integrations application. Customer policy states these developers cannot be granted the System Administrator [admin] role. Which of these is the best solution for granting the appropriate access needed to complete development work m the HR application?

options.text: Grant them delegated developer role to the global application scope
Advise the customer this work must be completed in Production
Grant them delegated developer role only to the HR Integrations application scope
Submit an exception request to allow them to have the Admin role

questions.explanation: Granting the Delegated Developer role scoped only to the HR Integrations application scope gives developers the access needed to make subprod updates in that scope without requiring full System Admin. Scoping limits their access to only the HR Integrations app.

questions.stem: When an employee contacts HR, they speak in terms of lifecycle events. From an HR perspective, that event gets translated into several HR services that need to be performed. Of the following items, which would be considered a lifecycle event?
questions.explanation: Lifecycle events represent major employee life events such as onboarding, offboarding, or parental leave — 'having a baby' is a lifecycle event. Direct Deposit Setup, PTO Inquiry, and Tuition Reimbursement are individual HR services, not lifecycle events.

questions.stem: All ServiceNow web traffic uses which data protocol to ensure data is always TLS encrypted in transit.
questions.explanation: All ServiceNow web traffic uses HTTPS to ensure data is TLS encrypted in transit. HTTP is unencrypted; REST and SOAP are API protocols, not the transport security layer.

questions.stem: Scenario: Alex is a member of the HR Tier 1 group which grants him the HR Basic [sn_hr_core.basic] role. He is going to be out of the office for a few days and wants to use granular delegation to allow his friend Amy to complete his tasks. Amy is not yet a member of any HR groups, but hopes to transfer into HR one day. Will granular delegation work for this purpose?

options.text: Yes. Granular delegation will automatically grant the necessary roles
Yes. Granular delegation will automatically add Amy to the HR Tier 1 group where she will inherit the role.
Partially. Granular delegation will allow Amy access to the HR Tasks, but not to the HR Case itself.
No. Granular delegation does not change a delegate's access to records.

questions.explanation: Granular Delegation does not change a delegate's record access — ACLs still apply. Amy has no HR roles, so she cannot access HR cases or tasks even if delegated to. Granular delegation routes work assignment, not security access.

questions.stem: Which Lifecycle Event activity type enables you to manage the dependencies or order of activities within an activity set?
questions.explanation: Activity container is the activity type that enables managing the dependencies and order of activities within an activity set. Member activities inside the container can be sequenced with dependency rules.

questions.stem: If all Can Edit Journey permissions are selected on the Journey configuration, which of the following users are allowed to make changes to the existing Journey? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When all 'Can Edit Journey' permissions are selected, the journey owner (A) and the mentor (C) are allowed to make changes to the existing journey — editing tasks and stages. Employees and admins are not granted editing rights through this permission setting.

questions.stem: Lifecycle Events includes an activity set that can be used to cancel and revert work done in a lifecycle event case. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: The Rescind process is the activity set that cancels and reverts work done in a lifecycle event case. It allows HR agents to undo completed activities such as workplace setup. Reverse, Cancel, and Repeal are not the HRSD term for this feature.

questions.stem: When configuring a Lifecycle Event, which of the following is used to define the relationships between fields in various tables?
questions.explanation: Activity Field Mapping defines relationships between fields in various tables within lifecycle event configuration, enabling data to pass correctly between activities and related records. Trigger conditions define when sets run; LE Properties are system settings; HR Templates populate case fields.

questions.stem: Which of the following features allows employees to delegate their tasks to other employees for specific date and time ranges based on delegation rules?
questions.explanation: Granular Delegation allows employees to delegate tasks to others for specific date/time ranges based on delegation rules, supporting approvals and task assignments by table and condition. Role Delegation, Admin Delegation, and Task Delegation are not valid HRSD feature names.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of Journey designer?

options.text: It tracks the progress of Lifecycle Events and onboarding cases using the dashboards.
It creates templates for plan and to-do tasks that managers, employees, and mentors can access.
It manages the dependencies of activities within an activity set.
It combines Lifecycle Event cases and Journey Accelerator action plans.

questions.explanation: Journey Designer combines Lifecycle Event cases with Journey Accelerator action plans into a unified manager and employee experience. It does not independently manage activity set dependencies or generate LE dashboards.

questions.stem: Which Security control option uses the context of the data within the record to grant and/or restrict access?
questions.explanation: ACLs (Access Control Level) use the context of the data within a record — field values, conditions, and scripts — to grant or restrict access. Platform Access, Scoped Application, and User Authentication do not evaluate record data context for access decisions.

questions.stem: Which HRSD application automates and streamlines employee onboarding and other activities across departments?
questions.explanation: Lifecycle Events automates and streamlines employee onboarding and other activities across departments by orchestrating cross-functional workflows for employee journeys and transitions. Employee Center is a portal; HR Integrations syncs external systems; HR Performance Analytics measures metrics.

questions.stem: What are the functions of a journey template owner? (Choose three.)

options.text: Manage the order and flow of the journey stages and tasks
Create task templates for their audience in a simple, user-friendly experience
Add owners and approvers to journey configurations
Change only the task templates that they own
Maintain oversight of journey templates and approval flows

questions.explanation: Journey template owners A=manage order and flow of journey stages and tasks, B=create task templates for their audience, and D=can only modify templates they own. C=Adding owners/approvers is an admin function; E=Maintaining oversight/approval flows is not a listed template owner responsibility.

questions.stem: What variable type is included to configure the HTML document template?
questions.explanation: HTML document templates support Customized Variables. Unsupported types explicitly listed include Label, Masked, Multi Row Variable Set, Custom, and Custom with Label. Customized Variable is a supported configurable variable type distinct from the standard 'Custom' type.

questions.stem: Which plugin when paired with HRSD, delivers storage space, filing system, and functionality to purge and retrieve documents?
questions.explanation: Employee Document Management organizes, secures, and tracks employee documents with access control and retention policies — providing storage, filing, and purge/retrieve functionality when paired with HRSD.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to view confidential data associated with the HR Profile?
questions.explanation: The minimum role to view confidential HR Profile data is HR profile viewer [sn_hr_core.profile_reader], which grants read-only access to sensitive profile fields. HR basic provides general HR access; HR Admin and Manager have broader elevated access beyond the minimum required.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow feature is used to create pulse surveys?
questions.explanation: Pulse surveys are created using Listening Posts. Journey tasks of type 'Pulse surveys' are only available when Listening Posts is installed. Learning Posts delivers online courses; Employee Forums and Employee Forms are not features for pulse survey creation.

questions.stem: What is the role of Trigger conditions in activity sets?

options.text: It defines specific employees to the activity set targets.
It defines when the activity set should be initiated.
It defines order number for the activity set.
It defines the relationships between fields in various tables.

questions.explanation: Trigger conditions define when an activity set should be initiated — they specify the conditions under which the set becomes active during a lifecycle event. Audience targets which employees are affected; order numbers sequence sets; field mapping defines data relationships.

questions.stem: Which plugin is recommended when upgrading from the global version of HR to the scoped version?

options.text: Human Resources Scoped App: Employee Relations [com.sn_hr_employee_relations]
Human Resources Scoped App: Data Migration [com.sn_hr_migration]
Human Resources Scoped App: Lifecycle Events [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events]

questions.explanation: Human Resources Scoped App: Data Migration [com.sn_hr_migration] is the recommended plugin for upgrading from the global HR application to the scoped version, facilitating migration of existing HR data to the scoped data model. The other plugins are functional extensions, not migration tools.

questions.stem: Which portal allows employees to submit ethical violation complaints?
questions.explanation: Employees submit ethical violation complaints via the Employee Center portal (or the Anonymous Report Center). Complaints are submitted as universal requests through Employee Center Quick Links and triaged by routing agents. Lifecycle Events, HR Performance Analytics, and HR Integrations do not provide complaint submission portals.

questions.stem: When creating a new Lifecycle Event activity set, what happens when the audience field is set as empty?

options.text: The activity set applies to all employees.
The activity set applies for a specific group of people.
